_pdu() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

use clap_builder::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, ValueHint, value_parser};

fn main() {
    let mut cmd = Command::new("pdu")
        .version("0.21.1")
        .about("Summarize disk usage of the set of files, recursively for directories.")
        .long_about("Summarize disk usage of the set of files, recursively for directories.\n\nCopyright: Apache-2.0 © 2021 Hoàng Văn Khải <https://github.com/KSXGitHub/>\nSponsor: https://github.com/sponsors/KSXGitHub")
        .after_long_help("Examples:\n    Show disk usage chart of current working directory\n    $ pdu\n\n    Show disk usage chart of a single file or directory\n    $ pdu path/to/file/or/directory\n\n    Compare disk usages of multiple files and/or directories\n    $ pdu file.txt dir/\n\n    Show chart in apparent sizes instead of block sizes\n    $ pdu --quantity=apparent-size\n\n    Detect and subtract the sizes of hardlinks from their parent nodes\n    $ pdu --deduplicate-hardlinks\n\n    Show sizes in plain numbers instead of metric units\n    $ pdu --bytes-format=plain\n\n    Show sizes in base 2¹⁰ units (binary) instead of base 10³ units (metric)\n    $ pdu --bytes-format=binary\n\n    Show disk usage chart of all entries regardless of size\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0\n\n    Only show disk usage chart of entries whose size is at least 5% of total\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0.05\n\n    Show disk usage data as JSON instead of chart\n    $ pdu --min-ratio=0 --max-depth=inf --json-output | jq\n\n    Visualize existing JSON representation of disk usage data\n    $ pdu --json-input < disk-usage.json")
        .arg(
            Arg::new("json_input")
                .long("json-input")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Read JSON data from stdin")
                .conflicts_with_all(["quantity", "deduplicate_hardlinks"])
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("json_output")
                .long("json-output")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .help("Print JSON data instead of an ASCII chart")
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("bytes_format")
                .short('b')
                .long("bytes-format")
                .value_name("BYTES_FORMAT")
                .default_value("metric")

After thorough behavioral analysis, I implemented a Rust binary that reproduces `pdu`'s exact CLI, error handling, JSON and chart visualization.

**Understanding:**
- Quantity is measured via `symlink_metadata`: apparent-size = len, block-size = blocks*512, block-count = blocks; directories contribute own size plus children.
- Hardlink deduplication counts each inode once globally using a post-order merge that subtracts duplicate sizes, and produces `shared.details`/`summary` compatible with original; paths order is intentionally left non-deterministic as original shows randomness from parallel traversal.
- Errors are reported to stderr wrapped in `\r\r … \n\r\r` with operations `symlink_metadata` and `read_dir`; `--silent-errors` suppresses them. JSON input conflicts with files produce exit 4, deserialization failures exit 3.
- Chart visualizer groups formatted sizes by presence of unit (metric/binary), right-aligns within groups, then pads to overall max plus 3 spaces (1 for root). Tree drawing uses bottom-up post-order ascending (top-down pre-order descending) with `┌──/├──/┌─┴/├─┴/└──/└─┬/├─┬` connectors and prefix `│ `/`  ` based on first/last child flags. Bar rendering computes rounded filled lengths per ancestor chain (`round(size/total*bar_width)`), then paints `█` for own, `░` for depth 2 ancestors, `▒` for depth 3, `▓` for depth ≥4, spaces beyond root, merging adjacent same-char segments; align-right reverses the bar.

**Artifacts:** `compile.sh` builds offline using cached crates (`clap_builder`, `serde`, `serde_json`) and copies `target/release/executable` to `./executable`.
